status: predeclared before additional production optimization; not an acceptance result
comparison: same-device candidate versus refreshed accepted Rust and unchanged qualified Python; no cross-device ratios

sampling.uncertainty: Use existing process-level envelopes and predeclared paired-process controls where needed; retain all runs and do not widen thresholds. Shared Python reports are not independent duplicates.

quality: Unchanged Phase 1/2 tolerances, artifact and oracle pins, all traces, exact IDs/ties, snapshots, tokenizer goldens and rejection tests. Additional regression cases supplement existing qualification.
resources: Record CPU/allocation diagnostics and lifecycle separately from acceptance wall timing. CUDA pool/Torch allocator counters and MLX active/cache versus RSS have different coverage. No hidden output, validation, precision or memory tradeoff.
promotion: Passing non-inferiority alone is insufficient: retain only reproducibly useful changes with acceptable complexity. Record experiment and escalation dispositions, including negative/no-go results.
order: Complete Linux/CUDA implementation and validation before Apple/MLX; shared follow-ups return through Linux. Both gates are required before closure.
stop_rule: Missing evidence, unresolved uncertainty, unavailable resources or required contract changes keep Phase 2 open. Ask the user with evidence and alternatives; Phase 3 requires separate authorization.
